ip_top_stories.title: US Judge Approves Anthropic's $1.5 Billion Settlement of Copyright Lawsuit
ip_top_stories.summary: A US judge has granted final approval to Anthropic's $1.5 billion settlement with authors and publishers over the unauthorised use of copyrighted books to train its AI systems. The deal is the first major AI copyright case to reach settlement and is described as a landmark moment in AI intellectual property law. However, the core legal question of whether AI training on copyrighted material constitutes fair use remains unresolved.

ip_top_stories.title: Sony Names 30,000 Songs in Expanded Udio AI Copyright Lawsuit
ip_top_stories.summary: Sony has significantly expanded its copyright infringement lawsuit against AI music generator Udio, naming 30,000 songs in the complaint. The case centres on allegations that Udio used copyrighted recordings without authorisation to train its AI music generation system.

ip_top_stories.title: Publishers Sue Google Over Alleged Copyright Infringement in Gemini AI Training
ip_top_stories.summary: A group of publishers has filed a lawsuit against Google alleging that the company used copyrighted content without permission to train its Gemini AI model. The case adds to a growing body of litigation targeting major AI developers over their use of protected works in training data.

ip_top_stories.title: China Issues Draft Regulations on AI Copyright Infringement
ip_top_stories.summary: China has released draft regulations addressing copyright infringement in the context of AI, signalling a move toward formal regulatory frameworks governing how AI systems interact with protected content. The draft adds to a growing international patchwork of AI copyright rules.

ip_top_stories.title: Indonesia Proposes Strict AI Regulations to Compensate Human Authors and Ban Imitation of Author Styles
ip_top_stories.summary: Indonesia is proposing a major copyright law revision that would require AI companies to compensate human authors and prohibit AI systems from imitating individual creators' styles. The proposals have attracted opposition from major technology platforms including Google.

ip_further_links.title: Who Owns the Copyright in AI-Generated Work?
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis of the unresolved legal question of copyright ownership in works generated by AI systems, examining current legal frameworks and their limitations.

ip_further_links.title: AI Labels Won't Decide Copyright Protection or Infringement, EU Says
ip_further_links.summary: The EU has clarified that labelling content as AI-generated will not in itself determine whether it is eligible for copyright protection or constitutes infringement.

ip_further_links.title: Australia Moves to Make AI Companies Pay for Energy and Creative Content
ip_further_links.summary: Australia is advancing proposals that would require AI companies to pay for both the creative content and energy they consume, as part of a broader regulatory push to protect Australian creators.

ip_further_links.title: Why Sony Just Filed a New AI Music Copyright Lawsuit Against Udio
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis of Sony's legal strategy and the broader implications of its expanded copyright action against AI music platform Udio.

ip_further_links.title: Hackers Expose How AI Music App Suno Stole Decades Worth of Copyrighted Music
ip_further_links.summary: Leaked information allegedly reveals details of how AI music generation app Suno sourced decades of copyrighted recordings for use in training its systems without authorisation.

ip_further_links.title: Courts Won't Settle the Fight Over AI and Creative Work: Politics Will
ip_further_links.summary: A commentary arguing that the fundamental disputes over AI and copyright are likely to be resolved through legislative and political processes rather than court rulings.

ip_further_links.title: AI Deepfakes Push Courts To Protect Identity Rights
ip_further_links.summary: Courts are increasingly being asked to extend intellectual property and identity protections in response to AI-generated deepfakes of real individuals.

ip_further_links.title: Artists Need Copyright Plus in the Age of AI
ip_further_links.summary: An opinion piece arguing that existing copyright frameworks are insufficient to protect artists in the era of generative AI and that stronger or supplementary protections are needed.

ip_further_links.title: Australia: 'Unethical' — Minister Admits Big Tech Firms Use Aussie Content Without Artists' Permission
ip_further_links.summary: An Australian minister has publicly acknowledged that major technology companies have used Australian creators' content to train AI without permission, describing the practice as unethical.

ip_further_links.title: Guest Post — Why Research Expectations Have Outpaced the Systems That Enabled Them (Part 1)
ip_further_links.summary: A Scholarly Kitchen guest post examining how the infrastructure of academic publishing and research is struggling to keep pace with the demands placed upon it, with implications for how AI tools are being integrated into scholarly workflows.
